Against the linearised 2h phi(alpha) the ratio at h=0.1 is 0.9987-1.0023 and at h=0.3 is 0.985-0.999 (the h=0.3 deficit is the curvature of the Gaussian itself: it is present at layer 0 where the law is exactly Gaussian). Answer: the true pre-activation law has 0.1-0.3% MORE mass near the kink than its Gaussian surrogate (with the exact mean and sd) at layers 1-12, falling to 0 (within 0.1%) at layers 13-15; the excess is the Edgeworth (skew+kurtosis) correction to within the 1e-3 resolution. Per neuron (h=0.1, N=32768, neurons with expected count >= 200): median 0.996-1.004 at every layer, 5-95% range 0.97-1.03 at layer 0 (pure binomial noise) widening to 0.90-1.04 at layers 13-15, i.e. a few-% per-neuron deviations for neurons with |alpha| >= 2 where the Edgeworth term g3/6 He3(-alpha) is a few % (such neurons carry little kink density: the kink-density-weighted ratio is 0.999-1.004 at every layer).
Sharper CDF version from the 2^20-sample cache (a_log table A3): P(z_a>0) - ndtr(alpha_a): rms over neurons 3.0e-4 at layer 0 (stat floor 4.9e-4) rising monotonically to 1.35e-3 at layers 13-15 (floor 2.4e-4), mean over neurons |<=| 1.3e-4; the per-neuron deviation correlates 0.87 (layer 1) to 0.995 (layers 13-15) with the Edgeworth (g3,g4) prediction; residual after the g3 term alone: 6e-4 rms (above floor), after g3+g4: 1.3-1.7e-4 (below floor: see caveat on shared samples). Mean |alpha| grows from 0.001 (layer 0) to 2.6 (layer 15); rms g3 from 0.002 to 0.11; rms g4 from 0.005 to 0.07.

(b) GATE STABILITY (N=16384, float64; perturbations x -> x + h e_c, c=0,1,2, and x -> x + h u, u uniform on the sphere; h=0.01,0.03,0.1). Flip fraction (x1e-4) is 0.97-1.17 at h=0.01, 2.9-3.4 at h=0.03, 9.7-11.3 at h=0.1 at every layer and every perturbation (table B1; layer 0 exact value 0.996/2.99/9.96 for e0, measured 0.999/3.01/10.07; stat error 2.4% at h=0.01). Exponent of flips vs h: LS slope 0.976-1.029 over all 64 (perturbation, layer) pairs; pairwise slopes 0.966-1.050; i.e. linear in h, as a finite density at the kink predicts. Comparison with the bound: flips / [exact two-sided small-ball event on the data, mean 1(|z_a| <= |dz_a|)] = 0.483-0.522 (all h, all layers; 0.495-0.505 at h=0.1); flips / rho_h(Gauss) with rho_h = mean_a 2 E|dz_a| phi(alpha_a)/sigma_a = 0.467-0.525; rho_h(empirical density from (a)) / rho_h(Gauss) = 0.998-1.004. So the companion bound C11 (P(flip) <= rho_h) holds and is attained at exactly one half: a flip needs z_a and dz_a of opposite sign, so P(flip_a) = |dz_a| f_a(0) + O(dz^2) = rho_h/2. Perturbation size: mean_a E|dz_a| = 0.034-0.037 h at every layer (the gated cocycle is norm-preserving on average), rms/E|dz| = 1.25 (Gaussian) for layers >= 1; dz is linear in h to 0.5% (E|dz|(0.1)/(10 E|dz|(0.01)) = 0.9952-1.0000, the deficit growing 0.03%/layer from upstream flips).

mechanisms.name: Small-ball mass of pre-activations vs Gaussian surrogate (the closure's kink-density ratio)
mechanisms.statement: Averaged over neurons, P(|z_a| <= h sigma_a) exceeds the exact-(m,sigma) Gaussian value by +0.1% to +0.3% at layers 1-12 and by 0.0 +- 0.1% at layers 13-15, for h = 0.003-0.3 (resolution 1e-3). The excess equals the Edgeworth prediction from the measured skew/kurtosis (1.001-1.003). Per neuron the deviation is a few % only for neurons with |alpha| >= 2, which carry negligible kink density; the kink-density-weighted ratio is 1.000 +- 0.003 at every layer.
mechanisms.where: a_smallball.py; a_big.log Table A1/A2 (N=262144) and a.log; cache-based Table A3 printed inline (session transcript)
mechanisms.status: CHECKED (Monte Carlo, N=262144 inputs, 1-sigma error 0.0007-0.0013 on the neuron-averaged ratio; alpha, sigma from the 2^20-sample cache, cross-checked against the fresh sample: sigma agrees to 0.6%, alpha to 0.005)
mechanisms.relevance_to_F1_F7: F6: the kink density phi(alpha)/sigma that sets the sensitivity law is correct to 2e-3 in the Gaussian surrogate when the surrogate has the TRUE mean and sd; the Gaussian closure's error at the kink is therefore dominated by its errors in (m, sigma), not by the non-Gaussian shape of the law near zero. The 2^20-sample CDF test sharpens this: P(z>0) - ndtr(alpha_true) has rms 1.35e-3 per neuron at depth (5x the stat floor), ~80% of its variance being the third-cumulant Edgeworth term, i.e. a closure that carries exact kappa3 per neuron (F1's chain) removes most of the per-neuron gate-probability error that a Gaussian closure with exact m, sigma would still make; the remainder is at the 6e-4 (kappa4) level per neuron.

mechanisms.name: Gate flip probability is linear in h and equals exactly half the small-ball bound
mechanisms.statement: For z_a(x) and the perturbed z_a(x+d) = z_a + dz_a, a flip occurs iff z_a lies between 0 and -dz_a, hence P(flip_a) <= P(|z_a| <= |dz_a|) (the companion's C11 bound with h = |dz_a|), and to first order P(flip_a) = E|dz_a| f_a(0) = rho_h/2. Measured: flip fraction per layer = (0.97-1.17)e-4 at h=0.01 scaling as h^(0.98-1.03); flips/exact-ball = 0.483-0.522; flips/rho_h(Gauss) = 0.467-0.525; rho_h(empirical)/rho_h(Gauss) = 0.998-1.004.
mechanisms.where: b_gateflip.py; b.log Tables B1-B5; exact layer-0 reference computed inline (ndtr(|dz_a|/sigma_a) - 1/2 = 0.996e-4 at h=0.01 vs measured 0.999e-4)
mechanisms.status: PROVED (the inclusion flip => |z_a| <= |dz_a| is immediate; the first-order formula follows from a finite density at 0 and sign-independence of dz from z) and CHECKED (N=16384, 4 perturbations x 3 h x 16 layers)
mechanisms.relevance_to_F1_F7: F5/F6: the gate (relu') defect under an input tilt of size h is linear in h with coefficient = kink density, so the Euler-Stein defect's kink content is first-order (Hermite degree-1-like) in the tilt, and the companion's concentration-function bound is tight up to the factor 2; the gated cocycle (F1) is stable: a tilt of input norm h moves each pre-activation by 0.035 h on average at every depth (norm-preserving transport), flipping 1e-2 h of the gates per layer.

mechanisms.name: Bulk hub pairing is exactly mean-zero in the last weight matrix
mechanisms.statement: P = (T A_b o T)(T C_b)^T with T = W_9 M is a homogeneous cubic in W_9; since the ensemble of W_9 is symmetric under W_9 -> -W_9, E_{W_9} P = 0 (likewise for P2, P3 and for the coherent part). Measured: ||mean P||_F / mean||P||_F = 0.1413-0.1423 for R=50 (null 0.1414) and 0.222-0.225 for R=20 (null 0.2236), for sample and Phi gates, real and random S_b, ages 1, 3, 6; entrywise-variance-normalised mean 1.01-1.03; cos_F between the actual-W_9 bulk and the resample mean <= 0.006.
mechanisms.status: PROVED (oddness in W_9) and CHECKED (R=50 and R=20 resamplings)
mechanisms.relevance_to_F1_F7: Confirms the mean-zero claim of F2 and F4 (Gaussian sketches of the hub index have zero mean on trilinear forms). Qualification: the coherent part lambda^2[2(a o b)a^T + (a o a)b^T] is also cubic in W_9 and is measured equally mean-zero (0.142), so 'mean-zero over the weight ensemble' does not by itself distinguish bulk from coherent memory; what does is that the coherent part is a function of two transported n-vectors and one scalar (O(n) data) while the bulk needs the n x n cocycle (F3's rank obstruction).

mechanisms.name: Size of the bulk pairing relative to the coherent part, and its self-averaging norm
mechanisms.statement: ||bulk||_F / ||coherent||_F at the actual W_9 = 16.1 (sample gates) / 11.6 (Phi gates) at age 3; 12.9 at age 1 and 25.1 at age 6 (sample gates); a random symmetric S_b of the same Frobenius norm gives the same numbers (16.2 / 11.5), i.e. the bulk pairing's size is generic in S_b. The Frobenius norm of the bulk is self-averaging across W_9 resamples (std/mean 0.7-1.0%) while the coherent part fluctuates 7%. The collective projection u9^T P u9 of the bulk (9.9e-3) is 2x the coherent one (5.0e-3); the diagonal of the bulk is 15x the coherent diagonal.
mechanisms.status: CHECKED (single network, one gate sample; Frobenius norms of the n x n (2,1)-slice readout at layer 9)
mechanisms.relevance_to_F1_F7: F2 (bulk pairing carries the memory) and F1 (marginal value decays with age): in Frobenius norm the bulk-to-coherent ratio grows with age (lambda/||S^off|| falls from 0.38 at layer 8 to 0.18 at layer 3), so older sources are even less coherent-dominated. Caveat: Frobenius norm of the readout is not the sensitivity of the output mean to it; the measurement does not re-derive F2's error numbers.

mechanisms.name: Identity P1 = P3 for the star legs
mechanisms.statement: Because C_b = A_b D_w2, the first and third bulk terms coincide entrywise: [(TA_b o T)(TC_b)^T]_{ij} = sum_r (TA_b)_{ir} T_{ir} (TA_b)_{jr} w2_r = [(T o TC_b)(TA_b)^T]_{ij}.
mechanisms.where: c_sample.log (||P1|| = ||P3|| to all printed digits); algebra above
mechanisms.relevance_to_F1_F7: Minor: the three star bulk pairings of Prop. (parts) in sec_transport.tex cost two distinct Hadamard pairings, not three, for the star block (the residual block's two terms are distinct).

mechanisms.name: Depth profile of the kink geometry
mechanisms.statement: Mean |alpha| grows from 0.001 (layer 0) to 2.6 (layer 15); only 504 of 1024 neurons at layer 15 have an appreciable small-ball mass (expected count >= 200 at h=0.1, N=32768) versus all 1024 at layer 0; rms skewness g3 grows 0.002 -> 0.11, rms excess kurtosis 0.005 -> 0.07.
mechanisms.where: a_big.log Table A1, inline Table A3 and the restricted-quantile table
mechanisms.relevance_to_F1_F7: F7: as the collective mode grows with depth the population splits into kink-far neurons (large |alpha|, few-% non-Gaussian density corrections that do not matter) and kink-near neurons whose law is Gaussian to 2e-3 at the kink.

caveats: 1. Resolution: the neuron-averaged small-ball ratio is resolved to 1e-3 (N=262144); per-neuron ratios only to 1-4% at h=0.1, so per-neuron non-Gaussianity of the kink density below ~1% is not tested by MC here; the sharper statement comes from the CDF test (gate probability, 2^20 samples), which is a different functional (integral of the density from 0, not the density). 2. In that CDF test the Edgeworth coefficients g3, g4 are estimated from the same 2^20 samples as pos, so the 'residual after g3+g4' (1.3e-4, below the 2.4e-4 floor) is contaminated by shared sampling noise; the g3-only residual (6e-4, above floor) and the 0.99 correlation are robust. 3. (a) compares the true law with a Gaussian having the TRUE mean/sd (from the cache); it does not measure the chain's own alpha errors, which F6 says dominate. 4. (b): float64 forward passes, N=16384; flips at h=0.01 have 2.4% statistical error; 'exponent' is from three h values only; perturbations beyond h=0.1 not tested; the bound compared is C11 with h = |dz_a| per neuron per sample, not a uniform h. 5. (c): T is taken from the post-activation space h_6 to z_9 (W_9 D(g_8) W_8 D(g_7) W_7) so that the gate at layer 6 enters once, through Phi in A_b; the tex's T_{l<-l'} includes an extra D(g_{l'}); this does not affect mean-zero-ness or the ratios materially. The residual-block bulk terms (R_b) were not included; only the star bulk (A_b, C_b) was paired. Gates from a single input sample (seed 99) or Phi; one network (net 0); one source/read pair per age. Frobenius norms of the n x n readout are not the output-mean sensitivity, so 'bulk is 12-25x the coherent part' is a statement about the slice, not about the final MSE. 6. Mean-zero in W_9 is a trivial oddness property shared by every part of the readout (coherent included); the measurement cannot discriminate F2's 'bulk is realization-specific' from 'coherent is realization-specific' - that distinction is dimensional, not statistical.
